page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top, with page number at the right. Main text in one column, with three marginal notes on the right (Rom.5.1, Luc.22.32, Mat.5.16). Below the text: a heading for the question "5. Qui sint conuersionis effectus.", a second paragraph, a decorative rule, the division heading "DE BONIS OPERIBVS.", then a woodcut-framed list of questions with its numbered lines beside the frame, running to the foot of the page.

main_text.p: na opera ex fide, tanquam ex fonte promanant. Rom.5.1. Iustifi-cati fide, pacem habemus erga Deum. Adiuvantes causæ conversionis sunt, Crux, castigationes: Item, pœnæ, beneficia, & exempla aliorum. Subiectum seu materia conversionis, in qua est mens, voluntas, & cor. 1. In mente & intellectu rectum iudicium de Deo, deque voluntate & operibus Dei. 2. In voluntate serium & promptum studium & propositū obediendi Deo, secundum omnia præcepta. 3. In corde boni & recti affectus. Obiectum est 1. Peccatum, vel inobedientia, nempe terminus ad quem. Forma conversionis est ipsa conversio, & conversionis accidentia. Finis conversionis præcipuus est gloria Dei. Finis autem proximus & subordinatus est bonum nostrum, beatitudo scilicet nostra & fruitio sempiternæ vitæ. Est & alius conversionis finis minùs principalis, Conversio videlicet aliorum. Tu conversus, confirma fratres. Luc.22.32. Sic luceat lux Mat.5.16. vestra coram hominibus.
main_text.head: 5. Qui sint conversionis effectus.
main_text.p: Effectus conversionis sunt omnia bona opera, ac serium studium tum obediendi Deo secundum omnia eius præcepta, sine ulla exceptione, tum alios etiam con-vertendi, atque in viam revocandi. Peccant quidem sæpe conversi, seu fideles, verùm non defendunt pecca-ta, sed student ea magis magisque vitare.
main_text.head: DE BONIS OPERIBVS.

l.i: 3. An sanctorum opera sint perfectè bona.
4. Quomodo opera nostra, licet non perfectè bona, Deo placeant.

page.notes: Woodcut initial Q of "Quaestiones" is joined to the word, as printed in the frame. The drop cap E of "Effectus" is joined to the word. Several words are doubtful: "serium" (read as serium[?]; it may be ferium or a similar form) and "serium" in the first paragraph. Line 6 is cut off at the foot of the scan; only "An" is visible, so the rest of the line is not transcribed. The running head is printed with spaced capitals as "DE HOMINIS GRATITVD.". Marginal references are printed as Rom.5.1., Luc.22.32. and Mat.5.16. Small ornamental dots and marks in the margins are not text and are omitted. No catchword or signature is visible.
